headline: The group's claimed Expedia haul, broken down: 830 million loyalty rows, 58 million profiles, 333 million accounts; none verified.
summary: New source: Cybernews's first article on the claim (s007, Tier 2, dated Oct 9, updated Nov 10), which lists the group's claimed figures. c004 now gives that breakdown and notes that rows are not people; it stays Unverified (same outlet as s002, so still one source). c003 notes the Oct 9 date. No label change on any claim or the main question. Checked: no Expedia newsroom post or customer notice; no Form 8-K with Item 1.05 on EDGAR (latest 8-K Nov 4, earnings); no Qubole or Idera statement. Staleness check done: head, known, not known, figures and size still accurate. Privacy check done: no staff, researchers, reporters, plaintiffs or contacts named. The group's page was not visited.

headline: Chase, Visa and Mastercard confirm vendor incidents after the group behind the Expedia claim listed them; Expedia's vendor is still unnamed.
summary: New sources: Wiz (s004, Tier 3) and Sentra (s005, Tier 3) write-ups of the Oct 14 to 26 Qubole attack, now cited directly in c008 (still Reported; neither names Expedia), and BleepingComputer Nov 20 (s006, Tier 2). Added c011, n0n's claim that it carried out the Qubole attack (Reported; via Wiz's Nov 11 note and BleepingComputer), and c012, JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard confirming incidents at third-party providers after the group listed them (Reported; one outlet; no provider named, not tied to Expedia). c007 and c009 details refreshed. No label change on any claim or the main question. Checked: no Expedia newsroom post or customer notice found; no Form 8-K with Item 1.05 in Expedia's SEC filings (latest 8-K Nov 4 is earnings); no Qubole statement found. Staleness check done: head, known, not known, figures and size still accurate. Privacy check done: no staff, researchers, reporters or contacts named. The group's page was not visited.

headline: Expedia confirmed attackers got in through a compromised third-party data platform provider; a group claims a billion records.
summary: First build from Skift (Tier 2; partly behind a subscription) and Cybernews and The Seattle Times (all Tier 2, read Nov 22). c001 vendor attack Confirmed on Expedia's own statement to Skift and to The Seattle Times; no company page was found. c003, c005, c008, c009 Reported; c004 the billion-record claim Unverified; c006 whether customer data was taken and c007 vendor and method Not established. A larger figure of over 1TB in the sweep notes was not in either source and was dropped. The group's leak page was not visited. Privacy check done: no staff, researchers, reporters or contacts named.
